qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Massive scale and vertically integrated iron ore mining provide an operational cost buffer, but ArcelorMittal remains an undifferentiated commodity price-taker whose margins fluctuate with global steel spreads, iron ore costs, and Chinese export dumping. 5-year normalized ROIC is sub-hurdle at ~2.5-3.5%, far below the 12% cost-of-capital threshold.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). Capital-intensive commodity steelmaker with normalized ROIC of ~2.5-3.5%, failing the 12% hurdle. Entirely a price-taker on global steel spreads, facing intense Chinese export competition and heavy decarbonization capex requirements in Europe.
qualitative.evidence: Normalized ROIC averaged ~2.5-3.5% across 2024-2025. EBITDA per tonne contracted to $121/t in FY2025 as European steel spreads remained compressed by Chinese imports and elevated energy costs. Net debt rose to $7.9B in FY2025. The business requires billions in ongoing maintenance and decarbonization capex (DRI/EAF transition) while lacking pricing power over finished steel products.
